<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

While profiling Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid GDN + full attention, M-RoPE) on 4x Intel Arc Pro B70 with the decode XPU graph enabled, we found that multimodal requests decode about 0.5 ms/token slower than text-only requests with the same context length. The GPU kernel time per step is the same in both cases, so the gap comes from host-side work outside the graph replay.

There are two sources of overhead:

1. **M-RoPE decode positions are rebuilt on the host every step.** `_compute_mrope_positions_decode` collects one Python int per request and calls `torch.tensor(..., device=...)` on every decode step. On an in-order queue, this blocking H2D copy waits for the previous step to finish, so the overlap scheduler cannot prepare batch N+1 while batch N is running. Text-only requests do not take this path, which is why only multimodal decode is affected.
2. **The XPU fused GDN decode fills a mask in every layer.** `XpuGDNAttnBackend.forward_fused_gdn` allocates `torch.ones(bs, dtype=torch.bool)` in every linear-attention layer. This mask is constant, but it is recorded into the decode graph, so every replay launches one fill kernel per GDN layer (48 per step for Qwen3.8-27B).

## Modifications

- **`MultimodalInputs` / `ForwardBatch`:**
  - Add `MultimodalInputs.get_mrope_position_delta_on_device()`. It caches the per-request M-RoPE delta as a device tensor the first time it is needed.
  - The cache is invalidated together with the existing `mrope_position_delta_repeated_cache` whenever a session turn rewrites the positions.
  - `_compute_mrope_positions_decode` now builds the batch deltas from these device tensors (a slice for `bs == 1`, otherwise `torch.cat`) instead of host ints. The integer arithmetic is unchanged, so the resulting positions are bit-identical.
- **`XpuGDNAttnBackend`**
  - Allocate the all-true `has_initial_state` mask once at backend init, sized to the request pool, and slice it during decode.
  - If a batch is larger than the pool, fall back to allocating a new tensor as before.

No behavior change is intended, and no new flags or environment variables are added.

## Accuracy Tests

The M-RoPE change only moves the same int64 arithmetic (`delta - 1 + seq_len`) from host to device, and the GDN change replaces a freshly allocated all-true mask with a persistent all-true mask. Neither change alters any numerical value fed into the model.

We compared greedy outputs (`temperature=0`) between upstream `main` and this branch, running both in the same image:

| Workload | baseline vs. patched | patched vs. patched (rerun) |
|---|---|---|
| 1080p image + 32K text, 5 requests, 1K output | identical | identical |
| 1080p image + 16K text, 5 requests, 1K output | differs | **also differs** |

On the 16K workload, two runs of the *same* patched build also diverge from each other. The prompts are random tokens, which gives near-flat logits, so run-to-run floating-point nondeterminism is enough to flip the argmax. The divergence therefore does not come from this change.

<!-- TODO: attach an sgl-eval multimodal accuracy run (e.g. MMMU) before/after if reviewers request it. -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Setup:**
- Hardware and parallelism: Qwen3.8-27B (bf16), TP4 on 4x Intel Arc Pro B70.
- Version: upstream `main` @ `019008afe0`.
- Workload: concurrency 1, one 1080p image plus 16K or 32K text, 1K output tokens.
- Method: baseline and patched builds were run in the same Docker image, swapping only the changed files; each configuration was run twice and the two runs differ by less than 0.02 ms TPOT.

Server:

    sglang serve --trust-remote-code --device xpu --model-path Qwen3.8-27B --tp 4 \
      --attention-backend intel_xpu --linear-attn-backend intel_xpu \
      --disable-radix-cache --disable-custom-all-reduce \
      --context-length 40960 --max-running-requests 1 --mem-fraction-static 0.55 \
      --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 \
      --cuda-graph-backend-decode full --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 \
      --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled

Client:

    python -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang-oai-chat \
      --dataset-name image --image-count 1 --image-resolution 1080p \
      --random-input-len {16384,32768} --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
      --num-prompts 5 --max-concurrency 1 --warmup-requests 1

Results:

| Workload | Metric | Baseline | + M-RoPE on device | + GDN mask reuse | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| image + 16K | TPOT (ms) | 27.57 | 27.02 | **26.96** | **-2.2%** |
| | E2E latency (s) | 31.48 | 30.92 | **30.86** | **-2.0%** |
| | Output throughput (tok/s) | 32.53 | 33.12 | **33.18** | **+2.0%** |
| | TTFT (ms) | 3278 | 3273 | 3277 | unchanged |
| image + 32K | TPOT (ms) | 28.05 | 27.53 | **27.47** | **-2.1%** |
| | E2E latency (s) | 35.04 | 34.50 | **34.44** | **-1.7%** |
| | Output throughput (tok/s) | 29.22 | 29.68 | **29.73** | **+1.7%** |

Profiling notes:
- Eager-mode profiling with `--profile-activities CPU XPU` shows about 26.4 ms of GPU kernel time per decode step, the same for multimodal and text-only requests.
- Before this PR, multimodal decode spent about 1.2 ms per step outside kernels, versus about 0.6 ms for text-only; after this PR the two match.
- `FillFunctor<bool>` (48 launches per step) no longer appears in the decode step.
- The M-RoPE change also applies to non-XPU backends; it has not been benchmarked on CUDA.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -16,6 +16,13 @@ class XpuGDNAttnBackend(GDNAttnBackend):
     as other platforms).
     """
 
+    def __init__(self, model_runner):
+        super().__init__(model_runner)
+        # Avoids one fill kernel per GDN layer in every decode step / graph replay.
+        self._decode_has_initial_state = torch.ones(
+            self.req_to_token_pool.size, dtype=torch.bool, device=model_runner.device
+        )
+
     def supports_fused_gdn(self, layer, forward_batch: ForwardBatch) -> bool:
         """Conservative guard: only the plain decode / non-prefix-cached,
         non-speculative extend cases are handled by the fused kernel."""
@@ -81,7 +88,10 @@ def forward_fused_gdn(
 
         if forward_batch.forward_mode.is_decode_or_idle():
             num_decodes, num_prefills = bs, 0
-            has_initial_state = torch.ones(bs, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
+            if bs <= self._decode_has_initial_state.numel():
+                has_initial_state = self._decode_has_initial_state[:bs]
+            else:
+                has_initial_state = torch.ones(bs, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
         else:
             num_decodes, num_prefills = 0, bs
             has_initial_state = forward_batch.extend_prefix_lens > 0

@@ -743,12 +743,21 @@ class MultimodalInputs:
     mrope_positions: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
     mrope_position_delta: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
     mrope_position_delta_repeated_cache: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+    mrope_position_delta_device_cache: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
 
     # Moss-VL related
     vision_position_ids: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
     media_nums_per_sample: Optional[List[int]] = None
     visible_frame_counts: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
 
+    def get_mrope_position_delta_on_device(self, device) -> torch.Tensor:
+        # Rebuilding this from Python ints every decode step costs a blocking H2D copy.
+        if self.mrope_position_delta_device_cache is None:
+            self.mrope_position_delta_device_cache = self.mrope_position_delta.reshape(
+                1
+            ).to(device=device, dtype=torch.int64)
+        return self.mrope_position_delta_device_cache
+
     def release_features(self):
         """Release feature tensors to free GPU memory."""
         for item in self.mm_items:
@@ -1730,6 +1739,7 @@ def _extend_session_image_inputs(self, image_inputs):
             self.multimodal_inputs.merge(image_inputs)
 
         self.multimodal_inputs.mrope_position_delta_repeated_cache = None
+        self.multimodal_inputs.mrope_position_delta_device_cache = None
         if positions is not None:
             self.multimodal_inputs.mrope_positions = positions
             self.multimodal_inputs.mrope_position_delta = (

@@ -1632,13 +1632,17 @@ def _compute_mrope_positions_decode(
             return
 
         if not has_precomputed_mrope:
-            # Compute all requests together to avoid per-request Python loops.
-            deltas_list = [0] * batch_size
-            for i, mm in enumerate(mm_inputs):
-                deltas_list[i] = mm.mrope_position_delta.item() if mm is not None else 0
-            deltas = torch.tensor(
-                deltas_list, dtype=torch.int64, device=model_runner.device
-            )
+            # Device-resident deltas avoid a host sync that stalls overlap scheduling.
+            device = model_runner.device
+            deltas_list = [
+                (
+                    mm.get_mrope_position_delta_on_device(device)
+                    if mm is not None
+                    else torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+                )
+                for mm in mm_inputs
+            ]
+            deltas = deltas_list[0] if batch_size == 1 else torch.cat(deltas_list)
             positions_1d = (deltas - 1) + seq_lens_int64
             self.mrope_positions = positions_1d.unsqueeze(0).repeat(3, 1)
             return
